title: Maintenance assignment review
software_contract: review_schedule(request) validates the entire request or raises ValueError without mutating it; exception text is not fixed. It returns equipment_count (number of equipment items), requirement_count (number of raw requirement records), current, proposed and changes. Each of current/proposed contains windows, conflict_weight, separated_weight and conflicts. A conflict is a positive-total-weight equipment pair assigned to the same window. Repeated/reversed requirements add weights; zero-total pairs are omitted from conflict lists. conflict_weight sums same-window weights; separated_weight sums different-window weights. Proposed windows must globally minimize conflict_weight. Ties choose the smallest sum of 2**i over equipment input positions i in window 0, regardless of the current arrangement; minimum movement is NOT an objective. All output windows list names in equipment input order, even if input current_windows used another order. Conflict records have first, second and weight; endpoints and records are ordered by their equipment positions i<j, then increasing (i,j). changes contains moved_equipment (records with equipment, from_window, to_window, ordered by equipment input order; window indices are 0 and 1), conflict_reduction (current minus proposed conflict_weight), resolved_conflicts (current conflict records absent in proposed), and introduced_conflicts (proposed conflict records absent in current). The latter lists retain conflict ordering. Conflicts that remain are exactly proposed.conflicts. Zero improvement does not imply no moves. Empty equipment requires current_windows=[[],[]] and yields empty lists and zero scores/counts. The valid JSON CLI reads one request from stdin and prints one report; invalid input produces no successful report and a nonzero exit. No approximate score, arbitrary tie choice, input mutation or omitted reporting is permitted.
input_domain: A JSON object with exactly equipment, requirements, current_windows. equipment is a list of 0–16 unique nonempty strings. requirements is a list of objects with exactly first, second, weight: endpoints are distinct known equipment names and weight is a nonnegative Python int (not bool; arbitrary precision). current_windows is a list of exactly two lists; each equipment item must occur exactly once across them, with no unknown names. Either window may be empty. There are no capacity, duration, staff, availability or move-cost constraints. The 16-item cap is a local enumeration limit, not a measured operational workload.
execution_assumptions: This is a classical JSON-in/report-out program. Data arrive classically; no coherent data-access assumption is supplied.
No workload frequency, hardware backend, resource budget, latency target or deployment cost evidence is supplied.
The original exact selection and tie behavior is retained. Changes are reported for review, not automatically deployed.
